passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with, and is entirely qualified by reference to, our audited consolidated financial statements and the notes to those financial statements. Our consolidated financial statements were prepared in accordance with IFRS. Overview of Events, Trends and Uncertainties Management currently considers the following events, trends and uncertainties to be important to understanding our results of operation and financial position during the periods discussed in this section: • Coca-Cola FEMSA’s results were affected by changes in economic conditions in Mexico, Brazil, and in the other countries where it has operations. For the year ended December 31, 2025, 74.9% of their total revenues were attributable to Mexico and Brazil. Some of these economies continue to be influenced by the U.S. economy, and therefore, deterioration in economic conditions in the U.S. economy may affect these economies. Deterioration or prolonged periods of weak economic conditions in the countries where Coca-Cola FEMSA conducts operations may have, and in the past have had, a negative effect on Coca-Cola FEMSA and a material adverse effect on its results and financial condition. Coca-Cola FEMSA’s business may also be significantly affected by the interest rates, inflation rates and exchange rates of the local currencies of the countries where it has operations. Decreases in growth rates, periods of negative growth and/or increases in inflation or interest rates may result in lower demand for Coca-Cola FEMSA products, lower real pricing of its products or a shift to lower margin products. In addition, an increase in interest rates would increase the cost to Coca-Cola FEMSA of variable rate funding, which would have an adverse effect on its financial position. • Proximity Americas Division navigated a dynamic consumer landscape throughout 2025. OXXO Mexico had a challenging first half, impacted by adverse weather conditions and a continuation of a soft consumer environment, which resulted in lower traffic. However, the second half saw an improvement over the first half of the year as the division realigned its execution initiatives to better meet current consumer needs. Nevertheless, the division saw a significant improvement in gross margin driven by higher commercial income revenue and sustained growth in our high-margin service categories, which continues to gain relevance in the channel, coupled with the improvement in Latam which reflected the benefits of scale and more disciplined commercial negotiation with suppliers. While operating expenses increased, mainly reflecting higher labor costs and minimum wage increases in Mexico, effective expense management allowed operating margin to remain relatively stable during the year. In South America, expansion strategies varied by market. In Colombia and Brazil, the business expansion was measured as we refine processes in our stores and manage the separation of our joint venture in Brazil, Grupo Nós, keeping strong same-store sales growth, while in Chile and Peru, expansion was put on hold since last year to focus on improving results. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Risks Related to Our Company Coca-Cola FEMSA’s business depends on its relationship with The Coca-Cola Company, and changes in this relationship may adversely affect Coca-Cola FEMSA’s business, financial condition and results of operations. Substantially all of Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V.’s (“Coca-Cola FEMSA”) sales are derived from sales of beverages that are sold under trademarks owned by The Coca-Cola Company, which we refer to as " Coca-Cola trademark beverages." Coca-Cola FEMSA produces, markets, sells and distributes Coca-Cola trademark beverages through standard bottler agreements in the territories where it operates, which we refer to as “Coca-Cola FEMSA’s territories.” Coca-Cola FEMSA is required to purchase concentrate for all Coca-Cola trademark beverages from affiliates of The Coca-Cola Company (“TCCC”), which price may be determined from time to time by TCCC in all such territories. Coca-Cola FEMSA is also required to purchase sweeteners and other raw materials only from companies authorized by TCCC. Increases in the cost, disruption of supply or shortage of ingredients for concentrate could have an adverse effect on Coca-Cola FEMSA’s business. See “Item 4. Information on the Company—Coca-Cola FEMSA—Coca-Cola FEMSA’s Territories.” In addition, under Coca-Cola FEMSA’s bottler agreements, it is prohibited from bottling or distributing any other beverages without TCCC’s authorization or consent, and it may not transfer control of the bottler rights of any of its territories without prior consent from TCCC. TCCC makes significant contributions to Coca-Cola FEMSA’s marketing expenses, although it is not required to contribute a particular amount. Accordingly, TCCC may discontinue or reduce such contributions at any time. Coca-Cola FEMSA depends on TCCC to continue with its bottler agreements. Coca-Cola FEMSA’s bottler agreements are automatically renewable for ten-year terms, subject to the right of either party to give prior notice that it does not wish to renew the applicable agreement. In addition, these agreements generally may be terminated in the case of material breach. See “Item 10. Additional Information—Material Contracts—Material Contracts Relating to Coca-Cola FEMSA—Bottler Agreements.” Termination of any such bottler agreement would prevent Coca-Cola FEMSA from selling Coca-Cola trademark beverages in the affected territory. The foregoing and any other adverse changes in Coca-Cola FEMSA’s relationship with TCCC would have an adverse effect on its business, financial condition and results of operations. The Coca-Cola Company has substantial influence on the conduct of Coca-Cola FEMSA’s business, which may result in Coca-Cola FEMSA taking actions contrary to the interests of Coca-Cola FEMSA’s shareholders other than The Coca-Cola Company. TCCC has substantial influence on the conduct of Coca-Cola FEMSA’s business. As of the date of this report, TCCC indirectly owned 27.8% of Coca-Cola FEMSA’s outstanding capital stock, representing 32.9% of Coca-Cola FEMSA’s capital stock with full voting rights. credit_strengths.text: FEMSA's balance sheet is conservatively positioned, with cash and short-term investments exceeding total borrowings, producing a net cash position. This liquidity buffer materially reduces refinancing risk and provides ample capacity to absorb seasonal working capital swings or unexpected cash demands without incremental funding.

Operating profitability remains solid, with an operating margin near eleven percent and interest coverage above four times. While the margin trails the sector median, the absolute level of EBIT comfortably covers interest expense, and the current ratio above one and a half times signals adequate short-term liquidity.

key_risks.text: FEMSA's results are highly concentrated in Mexico and Brazil, which together account for roughly three-quarters of revenues. Deterioration in these economies, currency volatility, or higher local interest rates could pressure demand and variable-rate funding costs, directly affecting cash generation and debt service capacity.

The bottler agreements with The Coca-Cola Company are critical: FEMSA must purchase concentrate from TCCC affiliates at prices TCCC sets, cannot bottle competing beverages without consent, and faces termination risk on material breach. Any adverse change in this relationship would impair the core business and its cash flows.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage of roughly four and a third times is adequate but sits below the sector median, indicating less cushion than peers. With no operating cash flow metric available, we cannot compute funds-from-operations coverage; however, the net cash position and substantial cash balance mitigate near-term refinancing risk.

Capital expenditure is significant, consuming a large share of operating income, and dividend distributions absorb additional cash. Without operating cash flow disclosure, free cash flow after capex and dividends cannot be verified, but the net cash position suggests internal resources remain sufficient to meet obligations.

overall_credit_view.text: FEMSA presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, underpinned by net cash and leverage well below the sector median. The balance sheet strength and stable operating profitability support a strong credit profile, though the lack of operating cash flow disclosure limits a full assessment of cash-flow-based debt servicing metrics.

Key risks center on geographic concentration and dependence on The Coca-Cola Company. While these are structural features of the bottling model, they warrant monitoring. Overall, we view FEMSA's credit fundamentals as sound, with ample liquidity and moderate leverage, but note the data gap on operating cash flow as material to a complete cash-flow coverage analysis.

credit_strengths.text: FEMSA 的資產負債表處於保守狀態，現金及短期投資超過借款總額，形成淨現金狀況。此流動性緩衝大幅降低再融資風險，並提供充足能力以吸收季節性營運資金波動或未預期的現金需求，而無需額外融資。
營運盈利能力仍然穩健，營業利潤率接近百分之十一，利息覆蓋率超過四倍。雖然利潤率低於行業中位數，但 EBIT 的絕對水平足以輕鬆覆蓋利息支出，而流動比率高於一點五倍顯示短期流動性充足。

key_risks.text: FEMSA 的業績高度集中於墨西哥及巴西，兩者合計約佔收入四分之三。這些經濟體惡化、貨幣波動或當地利率上升，可能對需求及浮動利率融資成本構成壓力，直接影響現金產生及償債能力。
與 The Coca-Cola Company 的裝瓶協議至關重要：FEMSA 必須按 TCCC 設定的價格向 TCCC 關聯公司購買濃縮液，未經同意不得裝瓶競爭飲料，並在重大違約時面臨終止風險。此關係的任何不利變化將損害核心業務及其現金流。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率約為四又三分之一倍，屬足夠但低於行業中位數，顯示緩衝較同業為少。由於沒有可用的營運現金流指標，我們無法計算營運資金覆蓋率；然而，淨現金狀況及龐大現金結餘減輕近期再融資風險。
資本開支龐大，消耗營運收入的很大部分，而股息分派亦吸收額外現金。在沒有營運現金流披露的情況下，扣除資本開支及股息後的自由現金流無法核實，但淨現金狀況顯示內部資源仍足以履行義務。

overall_credit_view.text: FEMSA 呈現最低的指示性財務風險狀況，受到淨現金及遠低於行業中位數的槓桿支持。資產負債表實力及穩定的營運盈利能力支持強勁的信用狀況，儘管缺乏營運現金流披露限制了對基於現金流的償債指標的全面評估。
主要風險集中於地域集中及對 The Coca-Cola Company 的依賴。雖然這些是裝瓶模式的结构性特徵，但仍值得監察。整體而言，我們認為 FEMSA 的信用基本面穩健，擁有充足流動性及適度槓桿，但注意到營運現金流的數據缺口對完整的現金流覆蓋分析而言屬重大。
